Dear Editors,

Please consider the manuscript “Central Frustration Obstructs Boundary-Uniform Local Control in Heat-Kernel Lattice Gauge Theory” as a regular article.

The paper proves a finite-lattice conditional-concentration theorem for heat-kernel lattice gauge theory. For any compact connected Lie group with a nonidentity central element, an explicit admissible boundary assignment makes a full-degree link see all but one identity staple and one central staple. The resulting conditional law has a compact-group metric-barycenter rate function. We compute the exact exponent for the frustrated plaquette to remain near the identity, prove that the obstruction persists on an open positive-measure boundary neighborhood, and show that the microscopic single-link Dobrushin row criterion fails at sufficiently small heat time.

The result addresses the quantifiers used in conditional rare-defect and product-domination arguments. It is not a claim of Gibbs nonuniqueness, confinement, continuum Yang–Mills construction, or a mass gap. The analytic proof is independent of computation; a standard-library exact incidence verifier is included as a reproducibility check.

The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. No external dataset was used. Author identity, affiliations, conflicts, and funding declarations should be entered in the journal system by the corresponding author; the enclosed PDF is blinded.

Sincerely,

The authors
